newsitem.title: GERMANY: German 1996 foreign trade seen up 4.1 pct-BGA.
newsitem.headline: German 1996 foreign trade seen up 4.1 pct-BGA.

text.p: The volume of Germany's foreign trade is expected to rise 4.1 percent to around 1.47 trillion marks this year, the German Wholesale and Foreign Trade Federation (BGA) said on Tuesday.
"If something is still growing in this country besides the budget deficit it's foreign trade," said federation president Michael Fuchs in a statement.
The volume of Germany's exports would increase five percent from a year ago to 787 billion marks this year, while imports would rise three percent to 684 billion marks.
After a slow first half, foreign trade volumes picked up in the second half of the year, Fuchs said.
Growth in exports was expected to accelerate to 7.8 percent to 405.2 billion marks in the second half after just 2.2 percent in the first half.
The strong mark and weak economies of important trading partners dampened demand for German goods in the first half, Fuchs said.

Sluggish private consumption in the first six months of the year slowed the growth in imports, up 2.2 percent to 339.3 billion marks. But the momentum has picked up and BGA predicted second half imports would rise 3.8 percent to 344.7 billion.

While expressing general confidence in the current economic situation, Fuchs added that Germany was in danger of falling behind in its share of global trade volumes, which the OECD predicts will expand some seven percent this year.
"You don't need a calculator to recognise that Germany is losing market share," he said.
